fact_rationales.F10: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is consistent with inferior myocardial infarction, which is a key feature of both R2.1 and R2.2.
fact_rationales.F17: Elevated troponin level is a marker of myocardial infarction, supporting R2.1 and R2.2.
fact_rationales.F19: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is consistent with R2.1 and R2.2, which involve myocardial infarction due to coronary occlusion.
fact_rationales.F20: Pericardial effusion and contrast present in the myocardium may indicate ventricular rupture, which is a feature of R2.3 and R2.4.

fact_rationales.F10: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF is more typical of myocardial infarction, particularly inferoposterolateral STEMI
fact_rationales.F17: Elevated troponin level is a marker of myocardial injury, which is consistent with myocardial infarction
fact_rationales.F19: Thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery is a common cause of acute coronary syndrome, specifically myocardial infarction
fact_rationales.F20: Pericardial effusion can be seen in cardiac tamponade due to ventricular wall rupture, but also in other conditions such as pericarditis
